rapport_notes: Warm and engaged, thanked her for the quick callback and kept a friendly, curious tone while itemizing a long inventory list.
process_discipline_notes: Nothing was repeated across stages; no open-ended rubric question was asked so no silence to lose.

evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — this is a callback continuing a prior inventory discussion; the customer raised no move-related concerns in this transcript for the rep to dig into (only logistics/process questions), so full credit applies per the rubric's no-concern-raised exception.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: "Then again, you only pay after the entire move is completed... you'll only pay for the hours actually [moved]." — covers pay-less-if-faster; commit-to-rate, window framing, self-prep tip, and 'does that feel fair' are not covered.

top_strength: Proactively surfaced easy-to-miss inventory (tool chest, plants, golf clubs, wall-mounted TV) with targeted follow-up questions, producing a much more accurate headcount/truck estimate.
coaching_note: The close only happened because the customer said 'let's go ahead and grab the reservation' — the rep should be the one driving the ask, and should work in the Save Your Ass lines (rate commitment, window framing, self-prep tip, 'does that feel fair' plus silence) before the customer gets there on her own.
